The official law page identifies the Norwegian Flag Act as dated 10 December 1898.

Section 4 gives Armed Forces naval use and permits the head of state and, with consent, other royal-house members to use the three-tailed flag.
The regulation specifies light medium blue fields and a golden-yellow cross, with NCS and CIE measurement details.

articles.factual_and_pedagogical_assessment: The final wording correctly preserves both legal forms and exceptions, while its visual-recognition advice remains appropriately limited to flag recognition rather than a uniqueness claim.

source_evidence.finding: Article 4 calls the national emblem a white-red-green tricolour of three equal rectangular bands: the first is vertical and white at the hoist, with the other two horizontal, red upper and green lower. It also names Antananarivo as the capital.

The official embassy page gives the same white-left/red-upper/green-lower composition and describes Madagascar as an island in the Indian Ocean, separated from the continent by the Mozambique Channel, with Antananarivo as capital.
